groups.instruction: In each sentence below, a four-letter word is hidden across the end of one word and the start of the next. The letters are always next to each other and always in the order they are printed. Find the hidden word.
groups.example: In “You must open a window.” the end of MUST and the start of OPEN run together as MUSTOPEN, which hides STOP.

questions.stem: The class made a photo advert to support their charity bake sale.
questions.explanation: The end of “photo” and the start of “advert” run together as PHOTOADVERT, and the four letters across the join spell TOAD.

questions.stem: Some geese eat early each day and still find plenty of food.
questions.explanation: The end of “eat” and the start of “early” run together as EATEARLY, and the four letters across the join spell TEAR.

questions.stem: Its fur was red, gentle underneath, yet warm in winter.
